quick_skim.title: An Automated and Reproducible Workflow for Crack Identification and Damage Assessment of Fusion Materials
quick_skim.abstract: Post-exposure microscopy is central to qualification of fusion materials. However, manual analysis does not scale to the volume, heterogeneity, and multiresolution character of modern fusion-materials campaigns. To address this challenge, we present a reproducible workflow, implemented in the Galaxy scientific workflow environment, for automated crack identification and quantitative damage assessment from scanning electron microscopy images. The workflow processes SEM images and experimental metadata to identify cracks, quantify damage, and retain the intermediate products and processing history needed for reproducibility. Outputs include crack masks, skeletonized crack networks, quality-control visualizations, and scalar damage descriptors. The method is designed to operate without image-specific parameter tuning across tungsten grades, microstructures, magnifications, and damage states. We demonstrate the workflow on a sparse electron-beam thermal-shock dataset containing 418 images from 114 experiments spanning five tungsten grades and three microstructural states. We define a crack-density descriptor, which provides standardized inputs for downstream machine-learning prediction and physics-based crack simulation. These predictive components are exposed in the same Galaxy environment and are intentionally treated here as extensible workflow modules. The principal contribution is therefore an end-to-end, shareable, and computationally portable workflow that links experimental characterization, automated image analysis, preliminary damage prediction, and simulation-guided data acquisition for fusion-materials research.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: A reproducible Galaxy workflow automates crack identification and damage quantification from SEM images of fusion materials, improving scalability and reproducibility of post-irradiation microscopy analysis.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对聚变材料辐照后显微分析依赖人工、难以规模化的问题，本文提出一套在Galaxy环境中实现的可复现工作流，处理扫描电镜图像与实验元数据以自动识别裂纹并定量评估损伤。流程输出裂纹掩膜、骨架化裂纹网络与质量控制可视化，并完整保留中间产物与处理历史。该工作提升了聚变材料后辐照检测的自动化程度与可复现性。
